boundary_note: Bounded first pass for both frozen records in Operations Against Vicksburg [December 1862-January 1863]. Preserve per-engagement dates: Chickasaw Bayou December 26–29, 1862, and Arkansas Post January 9–11, 1863. The live NPS campaign heading does not replace any battle interval. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the Army of the Mississippi and the Fort Hindman garrison; the live field reads zero. Greene says the garrison numbered about 5,000 under Churchill, quotes Sherman's letter that seven thousand were entrenched there, and says Porter's detachment carried 66 guns and the field artillery about 45 pieces.
claims.rationale: Garrison estimates differ between Greene and the Sherman letter he quotes; no Union infantry count is given. None is adopted as matched opening strength. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Greene says Churchill surrendered the fort to McClernand about 4.30 p.m. on January 11, with its 17 guns and stores.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. NPS's statement that the victory did not contribute to Vicksburg's capture is campaign context.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 6,547 total (US 1,047; CS 5,500); the live NPS field reads 6096 total (US 1092; CS 5004;). Greene gives Union losses of 977 (129 killed, 831 wounded, 17 missing) exclusive of 31 on the gunboats, and Confederate losses of about 200 killed and wounded with 4,791 prisoners counted.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Prisoners dominate the Confederate figures and are not an opening strength.

open_questions: Original returns, Churchill's and McClernand's reports, and the white flag's origin remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family; Greene is one retrospective history by a non-participant Union engineer officer, founded on the Official Records. Reports and letters quoted inside Greene are not additional independently inspected families.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
